summary: The referred HIGH finding from .rework/audits/fix_lm.json REPRODUCES at the current commit and is now fixed in src/train/api.py::process_setup. Reproduction, before any edit: two fresh CPU processes at RUN_SEED=0, LM_DROPOUT=0.2 reported torch.initial_seed() of 3695151007048800332 and 4263715014176632393 and LM.encode() over an identical zero batch summed to 3.682344 vs 4.750506 (gru arm) and -106.479309 vs -212.809799 (transformer arm, LM_LAYERS=2); the same pair at LM_DROPOUT=0.0 agreed exactly (5.071722 twice) and every model parameter agreed on every run (-19.315695), isolating the divergence to dropout drawn from torch's unseeded process-global default generator. Ruled under D11 in favour of option (a) -- seed the global generator in process_setup from run.seed -- but only WITH a declared read-back record, Process.torch_seed, which is what answers option (d)'s objection that a silent global mutation is exactly what the spine exists to prevent. Option (b) (a compose.py::RNG_SUBSYSTEMS entry) and option (c) (thread a generator to every consumer) were rejected on stated grounds, one of them measured. Both halves of the required measurement pass. The one filed todo item was already fixed at HEAD and no edit was made for it.

recommendation.chose: Option (a), REFINED: seed torch's process-global default generator once inside src/train/api.py::process_setup with torch.manual_seed(spine/rng.py::derive_seed("torch.global", int(run.seed))), placed before the tf32 writes so 'before any package is built' is literally true, AND record the result as a new frozen field Process.torch_seed READ BACK from torch.initial_seed() after the write. The read-back is the load-bearing half of the ruling, not decoration: option (d)'s argument -- that a silent global mutation is what the spine exists to prevent -- is correct, and it is answered by making the mutation a declared, checkable process setting rather than by declining to make it. That is exactly the shape Process.tf32_applied already has ('THE PAIR OF VALUES ACTUALLY WRITTEN, not the requested flag'), so the fix adds no new idiom. On the docstring's own phrase: 'the process-wide arithmetic settings ONCE, before any package is built' is NOT being stretched. A generator seeded from OS entropy is process-wide in the same sense tf32 is -- it changes nothing about WHAT is computed and everything about whether two runs of it agree -- and it is strictly narrower than tf32, which does move arithmetic. Two deliberate refinements to the patch proposed in .rework/audits/fix_lm.json's needs_shared_edit entry: (1) its LEVERS READ line spelled the new lever as 'seed -- <long prose>', which tests/test_contract.py::_split_items would have harvested as a non-identifier and DROPPED, so `seed` would have earned no K4 credit from this entry point at all; the shipped line spells it 'seed (<note>)' because the parser strips a parenthetical and keeps the bare identifier -- verified by running test_contract.stub_reads('src') directly, which now harvests seed for RUN. (2) The proposal had no DID IT FIRE surface at all for the new behaviour, which would have left a process-wide side effect with nothing to read it by.
recommendation.alternatives: (b) DECLARE "torch.global" IN src/spine/compose.py::RNG_SUBSYSTEMS so RUN.streams mints it like every other stream. Cost: a spine edit this package has no standing to make (and outside this task's ownership), plus a semantic cost that is the real objection -- that tuple is minted into a map the composition root SUBSCRIPTS to hand each package its own stream (compose.py rows for MEM.open_store, DOM.open_partition, WORLD.build, SIG.build, FAB.build), and tests/test_contract.py::check_k8_streams_are_declared exists precisely to keep those two in step. An entry no package ever holds puts a non-subsystem into a register whose documented three states -- 'a subsystem present with ZERO DRAWS is armed-but-inert; a subsystem ABSENT never asked' -- are statements ABOUT PACKAGES. It also breaks ordering: RUN.streams is the THIRD process row in ASSEMBLY_ORDER, after process_setup, so the seeding would move later than the function whose contract says 'before any package is built'. Rejected. (c) THREAD AN EXPLICIT generator= TO EVERY CONSUMER. Established as impossible at the installed torch, not assumed: at torch 2.13.0+cu130, inspect.signature(nn.Dropout.forward) is (self, input) -> Tensor, nn.TransformerEncoderLayer.forward is (self, src, src_mask=None, src_key_padding_mask=None, is_causal=False), and torch.nn.functional.dropout is (input, p=0.5, training=True, inplace=False) -- none of the three has a generator parameter. Doing it anyway means replacing nn.Dropout AND nn.TransformerEncoderLayer's internal attention/residual dropout with generator-aware implementations inside src/lm/api.py: a large arithmetic change to a package this task does not own, for a defect whose cheap fix is one line. Rejected as the fix, KEPT as the only thing that would close the residual coupling (see unfinished). (d) LEAVE IT AND MAKE IT REPORTABLE. Its argument is the strongest of the three and is the reason the chosen option carries a read-back field. But a Gate saying 'the forward pass is not reproducible at this configuration' is a true sentence that fixes nothing, and it would be UNREACHABLE-shaped in the worst way: the condition (LM_DROPOUT>0) is a lever the operator sets, so the report would say 'not reproducible' on every run that regularises at all, which is every run this project's goal A cares about. It also leaves G2's determinism floor -- measured from two identical seeded runs, tests/test_determinism.py -- absorbing a whole different dropout mask as float noise. Rejected as the whole answer, ADOPTED as half of it.
recommendation.evidence: 1. REPRODUCTION AT THE CURRENT COMMIT (2968aec), before any edit, through the real spine.assemble.build() pipeline and not a hand-rolled Config: two fresh CPU processes, RUN_SEED=0, LM_DROPOUT=0.2 -> torch.initial_seed() 3695151007048800332 vs 4263715014176632393; LM.encode(zeros(2,8)) sum 3.682344 vs 4.750506 (gru, layers=1). Transformer arm, LM_ARCH=transformer LM_LAYERS=2, same seed: -106.479309 vs -212.809799. CONTROL at LM_DROPOUT=0.0, same two-process protocol: 5.071722 vs 5.071722, identical -- so the divergence is dropout and nothing else. SECOND CONTROL: sum of all model parameters was -19.315695 in every process at every dropout setting, confirming src/lm/api.py::build_model's own named-stream initialisation was never the problem. 2. NOTHING IN THE TREE SEEDED IT: `grep -rn manual_seed src/ --include=*.py` returns five sites, four of which are gen.manual_seed on a PRIVATE torch.Generator (src/lm/api.py::build_model, src/sig/api.py, src/fabric/api.py, src/world/api.py) and the fifth is inside src/spine/rng.py::Rng.torch_generator. No call to torch.manual_seed existed anywhere in src/. 3. THE GAP IS TORCH'S, NOT THIS TREE'S: the three signatures quoted above, at the version quoted above. src/spine/rng.py::Rng.torch_generator's own docstring already says its Generator is 'to be passed as generator= to torch's random ops' -- there is no op to pass it to here. 4. THE SCOPE IS EXACTLY TWO CONSUMERS, checked rather than assumed: `grep -rn 'torch\.rand|torch\.randn|torch\.randint|torch\.randperm|uniform_|normal_|bernoulli|multinomial' src/ --include=*.py` finds every explicit torch random op already passing generator=, and `grep -rn 'random\.(random|randint|choice|shuffle|sample|uniform|gauss|seed)' src/ --include=*.py` finds NO live draw from python's global random module either (src/tok/api.py::_segment takes an explicit `stream`; the only hits are comments). So the global torch generator was the single unseeded stream in the tree, and python's global random needs no companion fix. 5. THE 'ONCE' CLAIM IS SAFE TO ENFORCE WITHOUT ENFORCING IT: src/spine/compose.py calls run_api.process_setup(run) exactly once (one call site) and tests/test_contract.py::check_k2_compose runs compose() once in a subprocess. derive_seed was chosen over rng_for anyway because it mints nothing -- verified: two consecutive process_setup calls in one process return the same torch_seed, do not raise, and leave spine.rng.issued() == [] -- so a process-wide settings applier does not acquire a new failure mode on a second call. 6. THE NAME IS A LABEL, NOT A STREAM, and the docstring says so, because this tree has already been bitten by the opposite: src/lm/api.py::build_model's own docstring named rng.issued()['lm'] as its firing surface after the draw had moved to the child 'lm.init'. 'torch.global' will never appear in issued() and the docstring tells the reader not to grep for it there.
recommendation.measurement: BOTH HALVES RUN, through spine.assemble.build() + RUN.process_setup + LM.build_model + LM.encode, in FRESH SUBPROCESSES, comparing a blake2b digest of the raw float bits of encode's output (not just its sum, so 'agree' means bit-for-bit). HALF ONE -- same seed must now agree: RUN_SEED=0, LM_DROPOUT=0.2, gru: torch_seed=3734753547471956429, encode_bits=84b871f99181a84c, sum=3.958331108 in BOTH processes. Transformer arm (LM_ARCH=transformer, LM_LAYERS=2), same seed: torch_seed=3734753547471956429, encode_bits=3045a3399f950969, sum=-65.768005371 in BOTH. Re-run after the final docstring edit: identical again. HALF TWO -- different seeds must still differ, which is the check that the fix is not the worse bug of making everything identical regardless of seed: RUN_SEED=0/1/2 at LM_DROPOUT=0.2 gru gave torch_seed 3734753547471956429 / 1763737848520504121 / 1486438900050504514 and encode_bits 84b871f99181a84c / 83b998193c737433 / 6bd748ed4429d933 -- three distinct seeds, three distinct torch seeds, three distinct outputs. Transformer arm at seeds 0 and 1: 3045a3399f950969 vs 9b2910c38d32bb3b. RUN_SEED=7 also distinct (3401938060292914317 / 9e9879a9d747b574). READ-BACK ASSERTED INSIDE THE HARNESS: `assert proc.torch_seed == torch.initial_seed()` holds on every run, and spine.rng.derive_seed('torch.global', 0) == 3734753547471956429 and ('torch.global', 1) == 1763737848520504121 confirm the reported value is the derived one and not a coincidence. WHAT IS NOT MEASURED: the CUDA arm. torch.cuda.is_available() is False on this box, so the claim that this also covers device='cuda' rests on the installed torch's own manual_seed docstring, 'Sets the seed for generating random numbers on all devices', quoted from inspect.getsource(torch.manual_seed) at 2.13.0+cu130 -- not on a run.

changed.title: Nothing in the tree seeded torch's process-global default generator, so at LM_DROPOUT>0 two runs at one RUN_SEED diverged and G2's determinism floor absorbed the difference
changed.what_changed: src/train/api.py::process_setup now reads run.seed and calls torch.manual_seed(spine/rng.py::derive_seed("torch.global", seed)) as its FIRST action, before the tf32 writes, so 'ONCE, before any package is built' is literally true rather than nearly true. derive_seed rather than a bare torch.manual_seed(run.seed) for the reason src/spine/rng.py::Rng.torch_generator gives in its own docstring -- one integer standing beside two different generators in every log is a thing no reader can check. derive_seed rather than rng_for because it is a pure hash that MINTS NOTHING, which keeps process_setup callable twice in one process and keeps spine.rng.issued() meaning what compose.py says it means (a register of per-subsystem streams handed to packages). No wire was added, no wire was needed: run.seed is RUN's own lever read by RUN's own entry point, so nothing crosses a package boundary and WIRE_BUDGET is untouched at 23/25.
changed.proof: BEFORE (current commit, no edits): two fresh processes at RUN_SEED=0, LM_DROPOUT=0.2 -> torch.initial_seed() 3695151007048800332 vs 4263715014176632393, LM.encode(zeros(2,8)).sum() 3.682344 vs 4.750506 (gru) and -106.479309 vs -212.809799 (transformer, LM_LAYERS=2). AFTER: same protocol, torch_seed=3734753547471956429 in both, encode bit-digest 84b871f99181a84c in both (gru) and 3045a3399f950969 in both (transformer). Seeds 0/1/2 still produce three distinct digests. Controls: LM_DROPOUT=0.0 agreed before AND after (5.071722), and the model parameter sum was -19.315695 in every process throughout, so nothing about initialisation moved.

changed.title: A process-wide mutation with no readable surface would have been the defect option (d) names -- Process gains torch_seed, read back from torch
changed.what_changed: src/train/api.py::Process gains a sixth frozen field, torch_seed: int, set from int(torch.initial_seed()) AFTER the write rather than from the number passed to the setter -- the same discipline Process.tf32_applied already states ('THE PAIR OF VALUES ACTUALLY WRITTEN, not the requested flag'), and for the same reason: the recorded defect it answers is a knob that reported itself off while cuDNN ran TF32 from its own default. The record's own docstring gains a paragraph saying why, and the module docstring's RECORD TYPES line now lists the field. This is what makes the chosen option a DECLARED setting instead of the silent global mutation option (d) correctly objects to.
changed.proof: `assert proc.torch_seed == torch.initial_seed()` holds on every measurement run above. dataclasses.fields(train.api.Process) now reads ['device','autocast','tf32_applied','amp_state','amp_reason','torch_seed']. Safe to add: `grep -rn 'sysm.process' src/spine/compose.py` shows the root reads only .device (six constructor sites) and never constructs a Process itself; `grep -rn 'amp_state|tf32_applied|Process(' tests/*.py` returns nothing, so no test reads the record; docs/04_CONTRACT.md mentions only `Process.device`, in the ASSEMBLY_ORDER produced-column table, so K1's signature check is untouched. Full suite green after the change.

changed.title: process_setup's frozen contract lines now match the body, and the new lever credit actually parses
changed.what_changed: LEVERS READ becomes 'device, tf32, amp, seed (...)' and DID IT FIRE becomes 'Process.tf32_applied, Process.amp_state, Process.torch_seed -- ...'. The lever is spelled with a PARENTHETICAL note, deliberately NOT with the '--' form the referred patch proposed: tests/test_contract.py::_split_items splits the block on depth-0 commas and keeps an item only if it matches [a-z_][a-z0-9_]*, stripping a parenthetical first, so 'seed -- <prose>' would have been harvested as a non-identifier and silently dropped -- the entry point would have claimed a lever the checker could not credit. Four new docstring paragraphs carry the ruling: the measured defect, why this function owns it and what was rejected, what it does NOT buy (reproducibility is not isolation), and that 'torch.global' is a derivation label that will never appear in rng.issued().
changed.proof: Running the real parser -- `import test_contract as T; T.stub_reads('src')['RUN']` -- now harvests RUN levers ['amp','bench','device','epochs','none','profile','seed','tf32']; `seed` is present, credited from this block. Every citation in the new prose is in path/file.py::symbol form and O12 resolves all of them (test_ownership: 12 checks + 18 self-test cases, 0 failing); no line number into a live file was written. No added line exceeds 100 columns (the five >100 lines in the file are all pre-existing, verified against `git show HEAD:src/train/api.py`).

unfinished.title: REPRODUCIBILITY IS NOT ISOLATION: torch draw order is still an undeclared channel between packages
unfinished.reason: out-of-ownership, and genuinely larger than this task
unfinished.detail: Seeding the global generator makes every run at one seed replay one sequence. It does NOT give each package its own stream: nn.Dropout and nn.TransformerEncoderLayer's internal dropout still draw from ONE shared generator, so a lever that changes how many masks LM draws still shifts every mask drawn after it -- exactly the confound src/spine/rng.py's module docstring exists to remove for the streams it does cover ('one stream, many consumers, order as an invisible coupling'), and exactly what tests/test_determinism.py's reference workload avoids by taking its generator from fab.torch_generator() 'never from torch.manual_seed()'. That sentence is about the WORKLOAD not drawing from the global; it does not argue against the global having a defined starting point, and this fix does not contradict it. Closing the coupling needs generator-aware dropout replacing both nn.Dropout and nn.TransformerEncoderLayer's internals inside src/lm/api.py -- LM's arithmetic, not RUN's, and a real change to what the model computes. NOT DONE, and deliberately NAMED IN THE SHIPPED DOCSTRING (the 'WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY' paragraph) so a reader of the L3 sweep cannot infer from the register's silence that the channel does not exist. Verified partial progress: the run-to-run half is closed and measured; the package-to-package half is untouched. Note also that no tests/test_lever_isolation.py exists in this tree yet (`ls tests/` lists only assemble, census, contract, couplings, derive, determinism, ownership), so nothing currently measures this channel either way.

unfinished.title: The CUDA arm of the fix is unmeasured
unfinished.reason: no CUDA device on this machine
unfinished.detail: torch.cuda.is_available() is False here, so every measurement above is CPU-only. torch.manual_seed is the right call rather than a CPU-only seeder because its own docstring at the installed version says 'Sets the seed for generating random numbers on all devices' (quoted from inspect.getsource(torch.manual_seed), torch 2.13.0+cu130), and it is lazy about CUDA initialisation so it is safe on a CPU-only box -- confirmed by the CPU runs, which neither raised nor initialised a context. What would settle it: one run of the same two-process protocol at RUN_DEVICE=cuda, LM_DROPOUT=0.2, on a GPU box, checking that Process.torch_seed matches and the encode digest agrees. That is a one-command check for whoever next has a GPU.
